claim: Ring all-reduce transfers 2(N-1)/N x message size and reaches near-peak interconnect bandwidth for messages over 1 MB.
quoted_support: The ring all-reduce algorithm divides the message into N chunks and performs N-1 reduce-scatter steps followed by N-1 all-gather steps. Total data transferred: 2(N-1)/N * message_size.

claim: NCCL's tree algorithm is reportedly 20-30% faster than ring for 128 KB-1 MB messages because O(log N) steps reduce latency.
stance_target: algorithm selection should be message-size dependent
scope_conditions: NCCL tree vs ring, 128 KB-1 MB messages
quoted_support: For messages of 128K-1M bytes, tree algorithms outperform ring by 20-30% because the O(log N) step count reduces latency.

claim: Manual NCCL algorithm/protocol tuning is claimed to yield 15-40% improvements depending on workload.
stance_target: NCCL default algorithm selection is not optimal
quoted_support: The library automatically selects algorithms based on GPU count, interconnect topology, and message size, but default selection is not always optimal. Manual tuning can yield 15-40% improvements depending on workload characteristics.

claim: A stated heuristic: communication-to-computation ratio should stay below 15% for efficient scaling at 1,000+ GPUs.
stance_target: communication overhead threshold for scaling efficiency
quoted_support: Communication-to-computation ratio should be below 15% for efficient scaling at 1,000+ GPU configurations.

claim: Ring performance degrades when spanning nodes without NVLink, which is the regime a PCIe-only box lives in permanently.
stance_target: PCIe-only fabrics are the worst case for ring collectives
quoted_support: Ring performance degrades when spanning nodes without NVLink.
